question.value: What is the spatial distribution and physical origin of deuterated water (HDO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and formamide (NH2CHO) emission in the SVS13-A protobinary system and its accretion streamer?

evidence.quote: We report ALMA high-angular resolution ( ∼ 50 au) observations of the binary system SVS13-A. More specifically, we analyse deuterated water (HDO) and sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) emission.
We investigate the origin of the molecular emission in the streamer, in light of thermal sublimation temperatures calculated using updated binding energies (BE) distributions.
The observations presented here have been acquired using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) on 2019 September 8 during the project (2018.1.01461.S, see also [1] ).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01461.S.
Continuum emission as observed by ALMA at 1.2 mm (color scale and contours) [1] .

findings_qualitative.value: Continuum emission at 1.2 mm reveals three elongated structures extending north from VLA4A and VLA4B, interpreted as dust accretion streamers feeding the binary system.

evidence.quote: In addition, we detect three elongated structures which extend from the northern edge of the continuum associated with VLA4A and B towards the north.
We conclude that the dust emission is tracing accretion streamers extending towards the north and the south and feeding VLA4A and VLA4B.

findings_qualitative.value: HDO and SO2 emission are associated with both VLA4A and VLA4B with an emission peak in between, whereas NH2CHO is compact and predominantly associated with VLA4A, confirming chemical segregation.

evidence.quote: As already noticed in [1], the NH 2 CHO emission is more compact and centered in VLA4A while HDO and SO 2 have a broader emission, extended also towards VLA4B. This finding confirms the chemical segregation reported in the binary system using iCOMs [1,18] .
The radial profiles show that HDO and SO 2 are extended in a region covering both protostars with a peak of emission in between.

findings_qualitative.value: HDO channel maps reveal a blue-shifted (+2.42–4.39 km s^-1) emission component at ≥ 120 au spatially coincident with the northern dust accretion streamer, with hints of NH2CHO at the same position.

evidence.quote: This component is perfectly aligned with the northern streamer traced by the dust, thus revealing molecular gas associated with the streamer itself.

In addition, the channel maps of HDO emission reveal a further component at blue-shifted velocities (+2.42–4.39 km s − 1 ) spatially coincident with the dust accretion streamer. The streamer traced by HDO is located at a distance ≥ 120 au from the VLA4A and VLA4B protostars.

findings_qualitative.value: Thermal sublimation at ≥ 120 au is excluded for formamide based on updated binding energies unless VLA4A is undergoing an active accretion burst; an accretion shock at the streamer-disk interface is proposed as the origin of the molecular emission.

evidence.quote: The presence of formamide at this position, considering the information on the binding energies and the corresponding sublimation temperatures (see 5.1 and Fig. 5), suggests that formamide is not thermally desorbed.

We find that a thermal sublimation origin of the molecular emission is excluded, unless the VLA4A source is currently experiencing an accretion burst. Alternatively, the emission morphology is consistent with an accretion shock, produced by an accretion streamer impacting the VLA4A disk, as previously found in more evolved protoplanetary disks.

findings_qualitative.value: In Class I disks, water is not necessarily confined to the inner 10 au.

evidence.quote: The spatial distribution of HDO in SVS13-A demonstrates that in Class I disks water is not necessarily confined in the inner 10 au, as suggested by previous ALMA and NOEMA H 18 2 O observations in 5 Class I disks [56] .

claims.finding: The northern and southern elongated dust structures trace physical accretion streamers feeding VLA4A and VLA4B.

evidence.quote: In order to verify that these structures are not artifacts introduced by the cleaning process, we test different beam tapering. All the elongated arc-like structures are still present when using a larger circular beam.
We conclude that the dust emission is tracing accretion streamers extending towards the north and the south and feeding VLA4A and VLA4B.

claims.hypothesis: SVS13-A exhibits chemical segregation between its binary components VLA4A and VLA4B.
claims.experiment: Mapped and extracted radial intensity profiles and peak integrated intensities of HDO 2(1,1)–2(1,2) and SO2 5(2,4)–4(1,3), comparing them with NH2CHO 12(1,12)–11(1,11).
claims.result: HDO and SO2 extend across both VLA4A and VLA4B (HDO intensity ratio VLA4A/VLA4B = 2.0 ± 0.6), whereas NH2CHO is concentrated on VLA4A (ratio = 7 ± 2), with no trend with line upper level energy.
claims.finding: Chemical segregation in the SVS13-A binary system is confirmed and does not strongly depend on excitation conditions.

evidence.quote: As already noticed in [1], the NH 2 CHO emission is more compact and centered in VLA4A while HDO and SO 2 have a broader emission, extended also towards VLA4B. This finding confirms the chemical segregation reported in the binary system using iCOMs [1,18] .

The radial and vertical profiles do not show a trend with the upper level energy of the different lines, confirming that the molecular distribution do not strongly depend on the excitation conditions [1] .

claims.hypothesis: The molecular emission (HDO, SO2, NH2CHO) detected in the northern streamer at ≥ 120 au originates from an accretion shock rather than thermal sublimation.
claims.experiment: Calculated thermal sublimation temperatures for HDO, SO2, and NH2CHO using quantum chemical binding energy distributions over 10^3–10^5 yr and compared them to the dust temperature (< 100 K) at ≥ 120 au for L_bol = 55 L_sun, alongside kinematic channel maps.
claims.result: Formamide's sublimation temperature exceeds the < 100 K dust temperature at 120 au, and HDO/NH2CHO show both blue-shifted (≥ 3 km s^-1) and red-shifted emission along the streamer.
claims.finding: The streamer molecular emission is likely produced by grain sputtering in an accretion shock at the interface between the streamer and the VLA4A disk, though thermal desorption cannot be completely excluded if VLA4A is experiencing an active accretion burst.

evidence.quote: We propose that the observed emission is produced by an accretion shock at the in terface between the accretion streamer and the disk of VLA4A. Thermal desorption is not completely excluded in case the source is actively experiencing an accretion burst.
Alternatively, the emission may be produced by an accretion shock, sputtering the grains, occurring when the accretion streamer impacts the disk of VLA4A.
We find that a thermal sublimation origin of the molecular emission is excluded, unless the VLA4A source is currently experiencing an accretion burst.

why_this_data.value: SVS13-A is a close Class I protobinary system at ~299 pc with known hot corino chemistry, chemical segregation, and dust streamers; high-angular resolution (~50 au) ALMA observations of HDO and SO2 clarify the origin of the elongated molecular distribution.

evidence.quote: SVS13-A is a perfect target to perform astrochemical studies and tackle some of the questions above. It is very well studied, in Perseus, at a distance of ∼ 299 pc ( Gaia, [11] ).

evidence.loc: 2.1 The prototype Class I hot corinos
evidence.quote: The origin of such molecular line distribution needs to be clarified using different molecular tracers. To this purpose we report here the analysis of sulfur dioxide SO 2 and deuterated water HDO in the SVS13-A system.

why_this_method.value: Evaluating thermal sublimation temperatures from updated quantum chemical binding energy distributions allows distinguishing between thermal sublimation from warm dust grains and non-thermal shock injection into the gas phase.

evidence.quote: In summary, the presence of HDO, SO 2 and NH 2 CHO, implies that either they (or their precursors) are thermally sublimated or they are injected from the frozen mantles into the gas-phase by a shock.
In order to distinguish which of the two hypothesis is correct, one has to evaluate the thermal sublimation temperature of deuterated water, SO 2 and formamide.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Cleaning artifacts as the origin of the northern continuum streamer structures (rejected via beam tapering tests).

evidence.quote: In order to verify that these structures are not artifacts introduced by the cleaning process, we test different beam tapering. All the elongated arc-like structures are still present when using a larger circular beam.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Chemical desorption or photo-desorption as the release mechanism for HDO (rejected as inefficient).

evidence.quote: Other possible mechanisms, such as chemical desorption or photo-desorption, would not be efficient here.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Thermal sublimation driven by an active accretion burst on VLA4A (considered possible and not completely excluded due to unknown individual protostellar luminosities).

evidence.quote: Thermal desorption is not completely excluded in case the source is actively experiencing an accretion burst.

In order to definitely exclude the possibility that thermal sublimation is responsible for the chemical enrichment at distances larger than 120 au, it is crucial to have an estimate of the individual VLA4A and VLA4B luminosities.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Self-gravitating substructures causing local temperature enhancements (rejected because the disks and circumbinary material in SVS13-A are expected to be gravitationally stable).

limitations_admitted.value: The blue-shifted part of the SO2 5(2,4)–4(1,3) line (at velocities < +6.5 km s^-1) is contaminated by the CH2DOH 4(3,1)–5(1,5) e1 transition at 241.61928840 GHz, making integrated SO2 intensities lower limits.

evidence.quote: The ratio is not reported in this case since the blueshifted part of the line is contaminated and the line intensity extracted in VLA4A is a lower limit.

Even if the blue-shifted part of the line (velocities lower than +6.5 km s − 1 ) is contaminated by the CH 2 DOH(4 3 , 1 –5 1 , 5 )e1 line at 241.61928840 GHz (see Table 1), the SO 2 emission in the other available channels shows a spatial distribution similar to that of HDO.

limitations_admitted.value: The individual bolometric luminosities of VLA4A and VLA4B are not measured separately due to angular resolution limitations at infrared wavelengths.

evidence.quote: The bolometric luminosity (L bol ) of VLA4A and VLA4B is not measured singularly due to angular resolution limitations at infrared wavelengths.

In order to definitely exclude the possibility that thermal sublimation is responsible for the chemical enrichment at distances larger than 120 au, it is crucial to have an estimate of the individual VLA4A and VLA4B luminosities.

limitations_admitted.value: Limited angular resolution of NOEMA DCN observations (1.2" x 0.7") prevents a direct comparison with the ALMA continuum streamers.

evidence.quote: However, the limited angular resolution of the NOEMA observations (synthesized beam of 1 . ′′ 2 × 0 . ′′ 7) prevents a proper comparison with the ALMA continuum emission.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only a single transition of HDO and a single transition of SO2 are analyzed, preventing an independent multi-line excitation or column density analysis at ALMA resolution.

Table 1 has a unit inconsistency between the table caption ('I_int (mK km s^-1)') and the column header ('I_int (K km s^-1)'); given the brightness of hot corino lines at 0.2" resolution (~349 K km s^-1), the column header (K km s^-1) is the intended unit.

The SO2 line is blended with CH2DOH precisely at the blue-shifted velocities (+2.4 to +6.5 km s^-1) where the HDO streamer component is most prominent, preventing kinematic confirmation of the blue-shifted streamer in SO2.
